title: MVVM without the boilerplate
cards/0/body:
View: the markup, only how things look.
ViewModel: what to show and what to do. Properties and commands, not a single control.
Model: data and business logic.

A ViewModel is easy to test: no windows, just C#.
cards/1/q: In MVVM, where should the "email is valid" check live?
cards/1/options/0: In the ViewModel (or Model), where there are no controls and testing is easy
cards/1/options/2: In a click handler in code-behind
cards/1/explain: The View only displays. Logic lives in C# classes with no UI.
cards/2/title: A generator writes the code for you
cards/2/body: Writing OnPropertyChanged in every property gets old fast. The CommunityToolkit.Mvvm package generates it at build time.
cards/3/q: A notifying property in one line
cards/3/explain: The generator creates a Title property.
cards/4/q: Why is the class marked partial?
cards/4/options/0: The generator writes the second half of the class: the properties and notifications
cards/4/explain: Your half has the fields and logic. The generated half has the properties.
cards/5/body:
A regular binding finds the property through reflection at run time: one typo, and the field is just empty. With x:DataType, Avalonia checks bindings at build time and generates fast code.

Avalonia 11 templates turn them on by default.
cards/5/code:
<Window x:DataType="vm:MainViewModel">
  <TextBox Text="{Binding Nmae}"/>   <!-- build error: no property Nmae -->
</Window>
cards/6/q: What do compiled bindings give you? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/0: Mistakes in property names show up at build time
cards/6/options/2: They work with Native AOT and trimming
cards/6/explain: You still need a DataContext. x:DataType just tells the compiler its type.
cards/7/q: Match each term to its role
cards/7/pairs/1/1: What to show and what to do
cards/8/q: The Avalonia template offers CommunityToolkit.Mvvm or ReactiveUI. What is the difference?
cards/8/options/0: The Toolkit is source generators and simple attributes; ReactiveUI is a reactive approach built on event streams (Rx)
cards/8/explain: The Toolkit is easier to start with. ReactiveUI shines in complex reactive logic.
